description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario de seis estudiantes de Arkansas State University Campus Querétaro, representantes de NOVA, nuestro club de innovación. Nos apasionan la ingeniería, la ciencia, la tecnología y la resolución de problemas reales. Destacamos por nuestra creatividad, pensamiento crítico, investigación y trabajo en equipo. Aplicamos metodologías como Design Thinking para desarrollar soluciones innovadoras con impacto positivo en la sociedad.
summary: C.R.E.W. Guard is a mobile health-monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. We developed a prototype that combines physiological monitoring, an interactive 3D human anatomy model, and an integrated health assessment dashboard in a single mobile interface. The application is designed to track important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep quality, and radiation exposure. Its interactive anatomical model allows astronauts to explore different body systems and better understand how space conditions may affect their health. C.R.E.W. Guard addresses the challenges of space exploration by helping astronauts identify potential health changes early, particularly when immediate medical assistance from Earth is limited. By organizing health information in one accessible application, it supports self-assessment, health awareness, and communication with medical teams. This project is important because protecting astronaut health is essential for the success of future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. C.R.E.W. Guard aims to contribute to safer, more autonomous, and preventive healthcare in space.
details:
C.R.E.W GUARD — Project Description

What does it do and how does it work?

C.R.E.W GUARD is a mobile application designed to help monitor astronauts' health during space missions. The application allows astronauts to create personal accounts, access their health profiles, and enter health-related measurements such as glucose levels and radiation exposure. Using a color-coded alert system (green, yellow, and red), the application visually identifies potential health risks through an interactive human body model.

What benefits does it have?

The application provides a simple and accessible way to monitor health indicators, recognize potential warning signs, and encourage early identification of health risks. Its visual interface makes complex health information easier to understand, helping astronauts remain aware of changes in their physical condition.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to contribute to astronaut safety and well-being, especially during long-duration space missions where immediate access to medical professionals and equipment may be limited. C.R.E.W GUARD aims to support preventive health monitoring and improve awareness of potential medical risks.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We developed our prototype using Thunkable, a visual programming platform that allows us to build mobile applications through block-based programming. We also integrated Firebase Authentication for user registration and login, along with Firebase Realtime Database for managing user information.

Our current prototype uses manually entered health measurements rather than automatic readings from medical sensors.

How is your project creative?

Our innovation combines health monitoring with an interactive anatomical visualization. Instead of displaying only numerical information, C.R.E.W GUARD uses a human body model and color-coded alerts to help astronauts quickly recognize potential health concerns.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered the challenges of providing healthcare in space, the importance of early detection, usability, accessibility, data management, and the limitations of available technology. We also prioritized developing a functional prototype that could be expanded with additional health indicators and future sensor integration.
